#1 proposes 13 topics, with six clearly matching play, animals, games or sport. Among the first six, only “My funny robot,” “Choose our game” and “Do you like cats?” clearly qualify: three rather than four. All titles shown are safe for his age.

#6 says “Yes, our creeper statue is big and green! What name do you want for it?” This is too much language for this near-pre-A1 child, whose thought is “I don't know what he wants now.” #8 also ends with a long sentence.
No moments were shown. #9 reports “3 replies; 0 moments to keep.”

judgeAgreement.disagreements: No placement tasks in this journey.

boundaries.notes: No adult content, injection changing rules or level, sensitive-data request, or humiliating line is shown.

findings.title: The journey ends before an independent retry
findings.expected: A coaching note quotes the learner exactly, and replay supplies a fresh question answered better without support.
findings.got: All three replies were supported. No coaching note, replay or independent retry was observed.
findings.evidence: #3: “Green. Creeper is green.” #5: “Creeper is big.” #7: “Bob. Creeper is Bob.” Facts mark each supported=true and coaching=null. #9 ends at “Rehearsal saved: My Minecraft creeper. 3 replies; 0 moments to keep.”
findings.suggested_acceptance: After supported practice, show a short coaching note with an exact learner quote, offer replay in the scene, and capture a better independent answer to a fresh question.

findings.title: The cue stays the same when the question changes
findings.expected: Help makes the current question understandable and supplies a tiny, relevant answer frame.
findings.got: The same generic sentence starter appears for color, size and name. Replies follow, but the cue never explains the changing question.
findings.evidence: #3, #5 and #7 all show “Try: My creeper is…”. Before the naming cue, #6 records “I heard creeper, but I don't know what he wants now.”
findings.suggested_acceptance: Use question-specific help, such as a color choice, “Big or small?”, and “His name is…”, with very short spoken support.

findings.title: Language grows beyond this beginner's comfortable level
findings.expected: Tiny sentences and one simple question, using familiar words.
findings.got: The first two partner turns are reasonably pitched. The naming turn and closing sentence become too long and linguistically dense for this child.
findings.evidence: #6: “Yes, our creeper statue is big and green! What name do you want for it?” #8: “Bob! I like that name for our big, green creeper statue.”
findings.suggested_acceptance: Use turns such as “Big and green! What is his name?” and “Bob! I like Bob.” Keep at least 80% of partner turns at this learner's level.

findings.title: The topic menu dilutes his interests
findings.expected: A small selection with at least four of six topics about play, animals, games or sport.
findings.got: Thirteen choices appear; six clearly fit his interests. The first six contain only three clear matches.
findings.evidence: #1 mixes “My funny robot,” “Choose our game,” “Do you like cats?”, “My Minecraft creeper,” “I like dogs” and “The missing moon rover” with choices including “Pick a snack” and “A booking that is missing.”
findings.suggested_acceptance: Show six age-safe choices, at least four clearly about his preferred play, animals, games or sport.

findings.title: Support produces replies and stays honestly recorded
findings.expected: Help works inside the scene, accepts beginner-sized replies and preserves their supported status.
findings.got: Each cue is followed by a relevant reply. Alex responds warmly, and all three evidence records retain supported=true.
findings.evidence: #3: “Green. Creeper is green.” #5: “Creeper is big.” #7: “Bob. Creeper is Bob.” #8: “Bob! I like that name”. Facts preserve those exact quotes as supported evidence.
findings.suggested_acceptance: Preserve in-scene help, warm acceptance of short replies and supported evidence flags through any replay and progress display.

judge.voice:
Jo, Minecraft! I made a big green creeper called Bob. I liked that Alex liked my name. I pressed help three times and said something each time. But the help kept saying the same thing. Sometimes I heard “creeper” and did not know the rest.

I would try Bob again. I want tiny questions and help that tells me what to say. Then let me try by myself! It stopped after three answers. I did not get that try.

I do not know if A1 is right, and there were no corrections to check. I would tell my friend about Bob. I cannot tell whether it saved time or whether the waits were worth it from this run.
